rounds.text: Indo Credit Capital Ltd offers a compelling entry point trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 1.25x on a book value of ₹ 8.13 per share [E2]. Furthermore, the stock trades at a slight discount on a relative basis, registering a price-to-book multiple of 1.24x compared to the sector benchmark of 1.36x [E7]. The market capitalisation sits at a modest ₹ 7.41 Cr, leaving significant room for valuation expansion as operational metrics improve [E3]. Demonstrating underlying operational recovery, the company's return on equity has successfully transitioned out of historical negative territory to positive figures of 1% and 1.03% [E9, E13, E28]. Conceded: [E1], [E4], [E6], [E12], [E25], [E26], [E27], [E52], [E60].

Indo Credit Capital Ltd trades at an extreme valuation that is completely disconnected from its underlying profitability, evidenced by a staggering P/E ratio of 124x [E1] that balloons further to 125.63x against a sector benchmark of just 20.12x [E6]. This lofty multiple offers zero income protection to shareholders, as the company yields a completely stagnant dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Operational returns are exceptionally weak, generating an ROA of a meager 0.6% compared to the sector benchmark of 1.79% [E8], alongside a pathetic ROE of 1.03% versus the sector benchmark of 5.11% [E9]. Long-term performance metrics confirm this is a structural issue rather than a cyclical blip, highlighted by a dismal 10-year median ROE of -2% [E25], a 5-year median ROE of -1% [E26], and a 3-year median ROE of 0% [E27]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio sits at a modest 1.25x [E2], and the stock sits at 72% of its 52-week range [E5], but paying a massive earnings premium for a micro-cap with a multi-year history of stagnant or negative returns carries severe downside risk.
